title: Swiss Pine: Ancient Swiss Pines You Can Visit
meta_description: A slow-growing Alpine pine that stops at the treeline: a Trentino giant a forestry worker refused to fell, a 1903 Berlin transplant, a Vilnius street tree.
intro: Pinus cembra belongs at the Alpine and Carpathian treeline, in the last thin soil before rock takes over, which makes every specimen at street level or in a city park a transplant rather than a native. Three are mapped so far. The oldest by story is Re Leone in Trentino's Passo Manghen, a cirmolo a forestry worker was sent to fell in the 1970s and refused, telling his supervisor it was a monument rather than timber. Berlin's grows on flat Dahlem sand, part of a 1903 teaching-garden planting nowhere near the two thousand metres of altitude this species normally needs. Vilnius keeps one three kilometres from its centre in the Antakalnis district, carrying the same edible seeds and dense, long needles as its wild Alpine cousins. Three cities so far.
